name: Gastric Linitis Plastica

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and clinical diagnostic criteria for gastric linitis plastica

criteria.description: Diffuse infiltration of the gastric wall by poorly differentiated signet ring cells with extensive fibrosis
Rigid, thickened, and non-distensible gastric wall with loss of normal rugal folds on endoscopy
Imaging studies (CT or barium swallow) showing circumferential gastric wall thickening with narrowing of the lumen
Progressive dysphagia, early satiety, and weight loss

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of histopathological confirmation of diffuse signet ring cell infiltration with at least one major clinical or imaging criterion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires correlation of clinical, endoscopic, imaging, and histopathological findings due to diffuse nature of disease.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Rigid thickening of the gastric wall
Diffuse infiltration by signet ring cells
searchTerms: cancer cells spreading in stomach lining

occasional.symptomName: Anemia secondary to chronic blood loss
searchTerms: low red blood cells from ongoing blood loss

rare.notes: Secondary to metastasis or lymph node involvement
searchTerms: jaundice caused by bile duct obstruction
skin and eye yellowing due to blocked bile

laboratory: Microcytic anemia due to chronic blood loss
Elevated tumor markers (CEA, CA 72-4) in some cases
imaging: CT scan showing diffuse gastric wall thickening with loss of distensibility
genetic: CDH1 gene mutations associated with hereditary diffuse gastric cancer syndrome
other: Endoscopic biopsy often requires multiple deep samples due to submucosal infiltration

distinguishingFeatures: Localized mass lesion rather than diffuse infiltration
Presence of glandular structures on histology
Hypertrophic gastropathy with enlarged rugal folds
Lymphoid cell infiltration rather than epithelial signet ring cells
May respond to chemotherapy and radiotherapy

redFlags: Rapid progression of dysphagia and weight loss
Non-distensible, thickened gastric wall on imaging
Histopathological evidence of signet ring cell carcinoma
references: Lauren P. The two histological main types of gastric carcinoma: diffuse and so-called intestinal-type carcinoma. Acta Pathol Microbiol Scand. 1965.
Van Cutsem E, Sagaert X, Topal B, Haustermans K, Prenen H. Gastric cancer. Lancet. 2016.
Kaurah P, MacMillan A, Boyd N, et al. Founder and recurrent CDH1 mutations in families with hereditary diffuse gastric cancer. JAMA. 2007.
